question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through `session_status`, or keep compaction behind sender/control-plane authorization until a different policy gate exists?
rationale: Source inspection shows the capability is missing and this PR is a narrow candidate, but allowing a model tool call to mutate active session context is a product and security boundary that automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Refresh the branch, keep the current-session-only checks, and accept `session_status(action: "compact")` as the approved model-callable boundary.

options.title: Require Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but add an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Continuation Design
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want broader continuation APIs to own voluntary compaction instead.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, keep the current-session-only checks, and accept `session_status(action: "compact")` as the approved model-callable boundary.
